description:
Private, offline editor for text, code, PDF, Word, spreadsheets and more. Omnitext opens practically any file you are sent, in one app. Instead of installing a separate app for each file type, often slow, with ads, upgrade banners, a mandatory account, or uploading your file, you get the right viewer or editor for each file: documents, spreadsheets, PDF, code, maps, subtitles, audio, video, archives and more. It opens quickly, saves back without breaking what it did not change, and never gives up on a file: anything unknown opens as text or hex. It is a private, offline editor that adapts to whatever file you open: code and data formats (JSON, YAML, XML, CSV, Markdown and more) in a proper editor, and PDF, Word (.doc/.docx), OpenDocument (.odt) and spreadsheets (.xlsx/.ods) in dedicated editors, all on your device. Opening, editing and saving a file runs entirely on your device. Your files are never uploaded, there is no account, no tracking, and no ads. Install it, turn the network off, and every format above still opens.
  • Edit PDFs: change text in place, add text and images, fill and sign forms (including complex government forms), redact, watermark, add bookmarks and attachments, pinch to zoom.
  • Edit Word (including legacy .doc), OpenDocument and spreadsheets, preserving the parts you do not touch.
  • Edit PowerPoint presentations: text, shapes, pictures, tables, charts, video, transitions and animations, with a slideshow and a presenter view.
  • Spreadsheets with charts, pivot tables, Power Query, conditional formatting, printing, freeze and split panes, form controls and VBA macros that run.
  • Code and data editor with syntax highlighting for many formats, and a tree editor for JSON and YAML.
  • Edit subtitles (SRT, VTT, ASS and more) and play video and audio with subtitles, including Dolby audio tracks and Apple Lossless.
  • Edit maps (GeoJSON, KML, GPX) and view many more formats: ebooks, 3D models, fonts, SQLite databases, email, archives (zip, 7z, RAR) and images, with on-device text recognition.
  • Command palette, light and dark themes, and version history to roll back changes.
Four optional features reach the network, and none of them starts on its own. Sharing a document, which you start yourself, sends it peer to peer to the people you invite, and the peers find each other through public nostr relays and public STUN servers (Google and Cloudflare by default, or your own); the document itself never goes to a server. The map editor can fetch background tiles from openstreetmap.org, and maps still open without them. The AI features (text recognition, translation, writing help, transcription) download their model once and then run on your device. The tiles and the model downloads each ask before the first fetch, and a refusal is remembered. The Check signature button on a health card fetches the issuer's public key from the issuer's website, only when you press it, and the button names the site. The app sends nothing else. Android's own web view, which draws the interface, may contact Google's autofill service on some devices; that is part of Android and cannot be switched off from the app. Free software under the MIT licence. The same app also runs in any browser.
